content_html:
Tao → I Ching → Select · Change · Reconstruct

This visual maps the Tao’s generative sequence to the I Ching’s symbolic grammar and to our memory workflow Select · Change · Reconstruct. It follows the Dao De Jing’s cosmogony (Tao → One → Two → Three → Ten‑thousand Things) and the Yijing’s combinatorics (yin/yang lines → trigrams → hexagrams).

Taoist cosmogony (Dao De Jing ch. 42) unfolds into the Yijing’s yin/yang → trigrams → hexagrams, which then map to a Select–Change–Reconstruct practice.

Tao → Differentiation (Select)

Tao gives birth to the One, the Two (yin/yang), and the Three. In practice, casting selects one patterned snapshot (a hexagram) from this flow.

Patterns → Transformation (Change)

Trigrams and hexagrams express ongoing transformation. Changing lines embody the principle that situations evolve.

Symbols → Meaning (Reconstruct)

Interpreting a hexagram reconstructs meaning: symbol meets context, making the Tao’s movement intelligible for action and alignment (wu wei).
